newsitem.title: UK: Britain condemns Serbian clampdown on protesters.
newsitem.headline: Britain condemns Serbian clampdown on protesters.

text.p: British Foreign Secretary Malcolm Rifkind condemned Serbian security police on Monday for injuring more than 100 pro-democracy demonstrators during peaceful protests.
"I deplore the violence used by police against peaceful demonstrators yesterday in Belgrade," Rifkind said during a visit to Sweden where he is speaking about European policy.

"The Serbian authorities must allow opposition supporters to meet and demonstrate freely. Violence will do nothing to solve the crisis in Serbia. The only way forward is for President (Slobodan) Milosevic to recognise without further delay the opposition victories in the November elections."

Police used truncheons and water cannon against 20,000 protesters who were demanding opposition victories in elections in 14 large Serbian municipalities, including the capital Belgrade, be restored. It was the 77th consecutive day the demonstrators marched in central Belgrade.
State television claimed the police took the action to clear the demonstrators who were blocking Brankov Bridge, which is one of the city busiest traffic spots.
France and Germany have also criticised Milosevic's handling of the protesters and warned that his continued intolerance of the opposition could harm relations with the European Union.
